readings: Link each invoice to its order and that order's customer, and count the number of distinct invoiced orders for each customer `gender` (a missing gender is its own group). Take the plain average of these per-gender invoiced-order counts. Then, considering only the genders whose invoiced-order count is above that average, give one row with the average of their invoiced-order counts and the average amount by which their invoiced-order count exceeds the overall per-gender average.
queries:
WITH gender_counts AS (
  SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS invoiced_order_count
  FROM Invoices AS i
  JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
  JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(invoiced_order_count) AS avg_count
  FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(g.invoiced_order_count) AS avg_invoiced_order_count,
  AVG(g.invoiced_order_count - a.avg_count) AS avg_excess
FROM gender_counts AS g
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS a
WHERE g.invoiced_order_count > a.avg_count
